sets.title: Player1
sets.summary: Camera mounts, protective parts, chase-camera setups and the skirt system, organized around the Player1 platform.

story.heading: Parts around a platform
story.text: The Player1 set includes camera mounts, arm protection, chase-camera pieces and a modular skirt system. The skirt files cover different power-wire exits, capacitor arrangements and receiver/antenna configurations.

story.heading: Moving to 6S
story.text: After losing an aircraft in Kauai, I planned a replacement around the Player1 frame and 6S power. My March 2022 build log sets out the priorities: a cleaner, stronger, simpler build with better power-to-weight.

story.heading: The LEGO edition
story.text: The July 2022 build brought my interest in LEGO into a Player1 aircraft. BrockLeeFPV designed the frame, and WoodChuck FPV cut it. The build log follows the frame collaboration, component choices and assembly behind the colorful exterior.

sets.credit: Player1 frame design: BrockLeeFPV. Frame cutting: WoodChuck FPV. This parts collection includes adaptations and reference models.

story.heading: Keep the spring. Add adjustment.
story.text: The housing and pusher reuse the Qidi Plus4 stock tensioner spring, adding screw adjustment to the spring load. I turned the concept into printable parts and shared the implementation with printing, hardware and installation guidance.

sets.credit: Concept and request: stew675 and spooknik. Printable implementation and original instructions: Michael Pytlowany / Jerky_FPV.

sets.title: Wardrobe replacement fitting
sets.summary: The corner fitting and latch from the PETG wardrobe repair.

projects.title: Keep the wardrobe. Replace the fitting.

story.heading: Repair the fitting, keep the wardrobe
story.text: A cracked plastic joint left an otherwise usable wardrobe in need of one replacement component. I reverse-engineered the fitting in Fusion and printed a PETG replacement to meet the existing rails.

story.heading: From the damaged part to the replacement
story.text: The corner fitting and latch are the model set for this repair. The project photographs show the damaged original and the purple replacement installed on the wardrobe rails.

image.alt: The printed wardrobe fitting installed on the existing rails.
image.caption: Installed fitting

projects.title: A lid that starts with the thread

story.heading: Start at the mating surface
story.text: This project starts with an existing jar rather than a free-form lid. I reverse-engineered its thread, recorded a 1/4-inch pitch and printed the translucent-blue prototype shown in the build story.

story.heading: Test piece and complete lid
story.text: The model set contains the thread-test version and the complete lid. The project photographs show the translucent-blue prototype fitted to the existing jar.

image.alt: The translucent-blue prototype fitted to the existing jar.
image.caption: Prototype photograph
